the THIRD read route: a Grep with output_mode content PRINTS the matching lines - measured live, a blocked Bash read of a settings.json was followed 8s later by a content Grep of the same path that returned its lines (count / files_with_matches modes print no value and pass)

the fourth read route: Playwright MCP's browser_file_upload hands a workspace file to whatever page asks - the Read judgement over tool_input.paths, matched by the tool's name under whatever server the user registered (audit 2026-10-14 PL3; the stack ships no browser server since 2026-10-24)

the project's sensitive data (<data root>/.secrets, .sensitive-data before; a dotenv the user fills by hand) by KEY only, and the run that uses it (--with-sensitive) - silent when there is none; every value is a credential there, so a Read is blocked, a dump masked and a source or copy refused

block *-implementer dispatch without its plan's data-root state/approvals/<plan id>/APPROVAL gate file (APPROVED/AUTO; the brief names the plan on a plan: line) or a root AUTO; and a dispatch, or a SendMessage that resumes a stopped seat, while ALFRED_CODE_MAXIMUM_RUN_AGENTS of the session's agents run (agent-cap.js)
the agent cap's registry: a started agent is counted (agent-cap.js), and a seat is told the session's number when it is not 5
the agent cap's registry: a stopped agent is marked, kept a while in case a hold sends it back

block a non-trivial git commit without the data-root state/approvals/COMMIT-GATE receipt (VERIFIED/WAIVED), and a git push or a change-request merge on any CLI or API route (gh pr merge, glab mr merge, az repos pr update --status completed, a curl PUT .../merge) without state/approvals/PUSH-GATE; a forge call forge.js cannot read is an ask, a deny when unattended (guard-ungated-commit:push in ALFRED_CODE_HOOKS_OFF turns that half off)

the publish half on every MCP server: forge.js reads the tool by its words (accept_merge_request, repo_pull_request_write with autoComplete, push_files), so a merge or a branch write through any forge server needs the PUSH-GATE receipt git push and a CLI merge do; a forge call with no known verb is an ask (a deny when nobody is at the terminal); every MCP server is judged (the stack ships none since 2026-10-24), a navigation, documentation or memory type's tool never a forge call (forge.js localTool)

Stop event: block a turn ending on a decision-shaped question in prose - re-emit as AskUserQuestion (measured stalls 13min-37h); also carries the fresh-session offer, past the window's absolute trigger, re-armed at 1.5x growth, and holds once a close after a fresh-session pick that carries no fenced paste text; and two log-only probes the analyzer counts - a done claim over a source edit (a file tool's or a shell write), unrun when nothing ran after it (guard-stop-contract:done in ALFRED_CODE_HOOKS_OFF off), and a close dismissing a failure ('pre-existing', 'unrelated to my change', 'flaky') in a turn with a red run or a skipped test (the red-run streak probe went with the shell-result wiring, deep hooks review 2026-10-16). Under an auto-run stamp naming this session, while the run's marker (`state/sessions/AUTO-RUN-<session>`) stands, a Stop is sent back to the run until its close deletes the marker - never the stamp, which only --mode-auto-run-off ends - held again only after a tool call (the Stop chain's workSince), and at most 49 times per marker: the 50th Stop passes with one auto-continue-cap row (audit 2026-10-14 HK05). Where the project compacts instead (ALFRED_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT=1) every fresh-session offer and note stands down, and an ask still carrying a fresh-session option is denied once, handed back with it dropped.

SubagentStop: hold ONCE a subagent that stops on a wait nobody will end (a first-person 'I'll wait for...' close or its own ScheduleWakeup call) while it started no background work of its own - the parent's history is not its situation (field report: a fork dropped its whole brief this way)

PreToolUse AskUserQuestion: FIX IN PLACE an ask whose own shape is mechanically wrong - its house voice (an em- or en-dash, a double quote), a fresh-session option quoting no number near the measured carry, a fresh option pointing at a resume block above that no fence shows - the corrected questions sent through updatedInput with no decision; DENY once per ask text, carrying any such fix, an option telling the user to type into Other, a single-select question without exactly one (Recommended), a new cycle's first ask with no fresh option; INJECT the judgement notes, which land beside the user's answer and are worded for it - stale scope (an option naming repo/remote/job state with no fresh read this turn: verify before acting, re-ask if it moved), a recommendation contradicting an un-actioned earlier prompt, the fresh-session offer for the next ask, a live credential. Presence only. Under a live AUTO stamp it ANSWERS an ask whose every question marks one (Recommended) option - allow plus an answers map in updatedInput - except a recommended push, merge, deploy or publish, and takes the next option over a recommended fresh-session hand-off; anything else waits for the user.
PreToolUse SubagentHandback: seal an output-scorer seat's report into its score file (mode-output-scorer); never decides

PreToolUse Skill: block a deliberate orchestration run starting on another run's carried history past the window-scaled trigger - route it through an AskUserQuestion fresh-session choice. AUTO-RUN (the stack-modes spec of 2026-10-27): `--mode-auto-run-on` leading the call's args on a task, capture, loop, issue or mode skill writes or keeps the session's AUTO stamp, never a run marker - only when the user's newest typed prompt is such a command whose leading run carries the flag (`modeFlags`; a prose mention starts nothing). Auto-run lasts the session: a message the user types mid-run is input to the run, a run's close deletes its marker, and only `--mode-auto-run-off` after a command ends the mode. COMPACT INSTEAD: under ALFRED_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT=1 nothing is offered or held; the session's first orchestration run and an automatic compaction's start are told the session compacts and goes on. BUILT-IN REVIEWS (the user's ruling of 2026-10-22, 'Stop the model using theirs'): the model's or a seat's call to bare code-review / security-review with no skill of that name on disk is denied, naming /review-code or /review-security, once the model can load ours (a personal or project copy skillOverrides leaves on - before update copies it, the built-in passes); guard-fresh-session-start:builtin-review in ALFRED_CODE_HOOKS_OFF switches it off.

the same run invoked as a SLASH COMMAND emits no Skill event at all (measured: 4 of 4 runs slash-injected, zero Skill events in 45 messages) - UserPromptExpansion fires on that typed command and names it; the matcher (a regex with no colon, which the row format splits on) lists the orchestration commands under either spelling - every task-* and loop-* name, a project's own and a digit included (audit 2026-10-14 HK06: a typed /task-migrate-v2 auto-mode never spawned it) - so no ordinary prompt spawns the hook; it injects the ask, never blocks (a blocked expansion shows its reason to the user only). The leading run of mode flags right after a task, capture, loop, issue or mode command (`modeFlags`, the stack-modes spec of 2026-10-27; a flag anywhere else is the task's text): `--mode-auto-run-on` writes or keeps the session's AUTO stamp, and each typed family command while it is live writes the run marker `<data root>/state/sessions/AUTO-RUN-<session>` and gets the auto-run contract instead of any offer; `/mode-auto-run <request>` is its own -on, and an old flag gets a pointer line and starts nothing. Every capture-*, issue-* and mode-* name spawns it too: each typed family command gets the MODE BANNER after whatever else it injects - two lines its first reply opens with, auto-run ON or OFF and how the session meets a full context (it compacts, or offers a fresh session at its trigger), with the window numbers.

every session start saves the `model` it carries under the session in <data root>/state/sessions/models.json, so the window is the model's own capacity from the first prompt on (the user's ruling of 2026-10-21: a settings alias like `sonnet` names none); on the `compact` source the harness just auto-compacted, which proves the session hit its compaction point at a moment a Stop may never come - leave a one-shot hold (a compact note where the project compacts instead)
a /model switch saves the `to_model` under the session, so the window follows the model the session now runs on before its next reply names it

the idle-gap offer: the prompt that ends a gap past ALFRED_CODE_FRESH_SESSION_AFTER_HOURS (the clock route's knob, default 2, 0 off) since the last reply injects the fresh-session ask once per gap, with the carry and cold floor, when a fresh session pays back with the cache warm (audit 2026-10-10 C09: a next-day resume ran 14 messages at 289.9k unoffered). A harness notice, a seat and nobody at the terminal get no offer

before a compaction, write <data root>/state/sessions/COMPACT-STATE-<session> (one per session) - the live plan, the active flow and its body path, the open flow stamps with their ages, the files this session wrote - with no model call; the compact SessionStart points at it

the post-compaction hold: after an automatic compaction the first changing call (a dispatch here, the first phase Skill call on the Skill row, an edit or a shell call on the two rows below) is denied once with the measured carry and cold floor until an AskUserQuestion is answered or the turn names a single short step - released when a resume would recover too little, when nobody is at the terminal (a live AUTO waiver included) or after two denials; with no hold pending the hook exits on one file check
the post-compaction hold on an edit - this row folds into the file-guard dispatcher, which runs the hook in-process (one process per file call, 2.1.5 M3)
the post-compaction hold on the shell route - a shell command after an automatic compaction is a change like an edit; this row folds into the shell-guard dispatcher (one process per shell call)

an EXISTING lint / format / analyzer config, or a strictness setting in tsconfig / MSBuild, cannot be changed to get a check green - creating one passes; the CONFIG-EDIT-ALLOW receipt honours a wanted change, guard-config-protection in ALFRED_CODE_HOOKS_OFF turns it off
same gate on the shell routes (an in-place edit, redirect, tee, rm, mv or cp onto the config) - run inside shell-guards.js with the other shell guards
one session, one project: block a WRITE that lands outside the project root (reads/investigation untouched) - the change another repo needs is handed off as a task card
same gate on the shell routes (redirect, tee, in-place sed/perl, cp/mv, rm/mkdir/chmod, git -C, cd then a write) - run inside shell-guards.js

the desktop servers' process launchers, matched by tool name under whatever server the user registered (the stack ships none since 2026-10-24): deny Windows-MCP App with mode launch_executable (any executable, caller-given args - the server excludes by tool name, never by mode) and every MacOS-MCP Shell call (a shell command no shell guard sees); App's launch / switch / resize pass; and a browser server's browser_run_code_unsafe (arbitrary JavaScript in the server's own process, no flag switches it off - 2026-10-24, ruling N9); the DESKTOP-EXEC-ALLOW receipt (App, Shell, browser_run_code_unsafe, an executable, or *) honours a wanted call

inject the answer budget (~3 sentences plus points) at the end of the turn's context - the short-answer rule mechanized; a correction turn writes one log-only probe row (ALFRED_CODE_CORRECTION_NUDGE=inject adds the save line - the preferences docs or Claude Code's own memory); rewrites the session-inspector status file when auto-run or the scorer changed

re-inject the budget after a COMPACTION rebuilds the context without it (measured absent for 277 of 366 messages in one session); startup, resume and clear get it from the first prompt's UserPromptSubmit injection, so the start no longer pays for a second copy (deep hooks review 2026-10-16)

an answer TYPED into an ask (matching none of the offered labels) is the user speaking: one ask-answer-typed probe row; a short one carrying a correction marker also writes the correction row (the same test and nudge mode as a typed prompt); one naming a path gets a note to open it and restate what it changes before acting (audit 2026-10-10 C15 / C07: corrections typed into asks were never counted, and a folder named in an answer was never opened). Never blocks
the architecture docs as the session's starting point: merged branches' doc versions folded into mainline, then the map's orientation block, this branch's overrides and how to read by section

the same orientation for a dispatched subagent - SessionStart context never reaches one at dispatch (a seat's own compaction runs SessionStart inside it), plus the snapshot the finish ask compares against

the finish ask for a seat that stopped WITHOUT a hand-back (a harness with no SubagentHandback tool, Cursor among them): what THAT agent changed, once - the seat that made the change is the only context that knows why

the finish ask, per agent, BEFORE its report leaves: the seat's first SubagentHandback that owes one is denied with the ask, and the retried hand-back carries the docs line (deep hooks review 2026-10-16: 48 of 48 SubagentStop asks came after the hand-back, 41 never acted on)
doc reads recorded; the FIRST change under a source root held until a covering section was read, that section handed over inline
the same hold on a navigation server's two edit tools (Serena's rename_symbol / safe_delete_symbol), matched by name under whatever server the user registered - the file is tool_input.relative_path

the same read record and hold on the shell routes - run inside shell-guards.js; every Bash|PowerShell|Monitor row of a guard shell-guards.js lists is wired as that ONE dispatcher (wiringRows), never on its own
once per session: a change that hit watch.json asks for the owning sections to be rewritten or confirmed

the user's preferences docs: the FIRST edit of each actor (the main session, each seat) held until the code docs that exist were read, the PERSONAL-CODE and ARCHITECTURE entries whose Scope: reaches the target and PROJECT-CODE's sections covering it inline, in parts past one room (a later edit a not-yet-handed entry or section reaches waits again); a judge's (a designer, a verifier, the code-quality analyzer, the security auditor, the integration reviewer), a handed architecture analyzer's and the main session's in a review run first reads (a Read, a Grep - its denial steering to the navigation server -, an LSP call or a symbol lookup) held while its start left entries unhanded, each handing over the next part; only a whole Read of a doc marks it read; a doc that is a link is never read; a seat's .claude/worktrees/<n>/ target is judged as the project path it mirrors - run inside file-guards.js
a judge's first LSP calls held like its first Reads while its start left entries unhanded, each handing over the next part - the filePath under the preferences folder never held

the FIRST git write of each actor (index, tree, ref, stash, a branch, tag or worktree branch made, a change request opened or merged, a release made - by concept, on any CLI or API route) held until GIT-PREFERENCES.md was read, handed over live with its locked entries first as the seed states them; one command that edits and commits shares one room, git first; a shell source write is an edit, a whole-file reader naming a doc (no head, grep or pipe into one) marks it read; a judge's, a handed architecture analyzer's or a reviewing main session's shell read of a file outside the preferences folder (cat, sed, head, grep, rg ... with a path argument on disk, through a variable the command sets, or as a glob an entry matches; a search given no path - rg reading no pipe, a recursive grep; a reader find -exec or xargs runs; a Select-String fed by a file listing - never wc or ls) is held like its Read, a grep word earning the steer line - run inside shell-guards.js

every MCP call, read by its tool name (the stack ships no server since 2026-10-24): a navigation server's two edit tools take the first-edit hold (the file is tool_input.relative_path), its five symbol lookups a judge's read hold (a seat that locates before it reads may never call Read), and a tool forge.js reads as opening or merging a change request, a branch write or a release (create_merge_request, push_files, repo_pull_request_write with autoComplete) the first-git-write hold, as the shell route does

PERSONAL-PREFERENCES.md pushed at every MAIN session start - startup, resume, clear, compact and fork, so it is back after each compaction; a compaction or a clear also deletes that actor's read record, so the held docs are handed over again - a compaction keeps the record's run and architecture hand-over, a clear ends them; a seat's own compaction (the payload carries its agent_id) deletes only its record and pushes only that seat's tool order. After the personal doc: the tool order (tools.js toolsLine) - each job's ranks from TOOLS-PREFERENCES.md, or the adapter table's defaults for a job it leaves out, resolved against what this machine reaches, each with its ToolSearch select: load line, and once per project with no doc the /capture-preferences tools suggestion; preferences-session:tools in ALFRED_CODE_HOOKS_OFF off; then this host's shell traps (win32: the Git Bash line; a zsh $SHELL: the two zsh lines - audit 2026-10-14 RU13, moved here from the retired memory-session.js), at a seat's own compaction too; preferences-session:host in ALFRED_CODE_HOOKS_OFF drops them alone

a judge - a solution designer or a verifier (agent_type ending solution-designer or -verifier), or a finding seat (code-quality-analyzer, security-auditor, integration-reviewer) - has no edit tool, so no edit hold reaches it: the code docs are handed over at its start, every project-doc section as far as the one room fits, and marked in its record; the entries the room could not hold come with its first reads (a Read, a Grep, an LSP call or a symbol lookup). The architecture analyzer is handed ARCHITECTURE-PREFERENCES.md alone, and told to report a departure as a smell naming its id, only inside an architecture quality run (the main session's run, below) - the map capture dispatches the same seat to describe the code as it is. alfred-code:<seat> always; a bare name only where the install stamp's library-agents: line records its copy, so a project's own agent or another plugin's seat of the same name gets no docs. Every seat but Claude Code's two guides is told its tool order after any doc push: a seat whose definition the hook finds (the core's own, a project copy) only the ranks its tools: and disallowedTools: grant, with no load line, any other the main session's; then, for every seat, this host's shell traps (preferences-session:host off)

the main session's run: a Skill call naming a capture-, loop-, task- or issue- skill, review-code or review-security (or the built-in code-review / security-review a user types; bare) is recorded as the run, with where the transcript stood - the run ends at the user's next typed turn other than a go-on reply (continue, go on, yes, ok ...), read only at an analyzer's start and a reviewing main session's held read; a review run's (review-code, review-security, the built-in two, the code and architecture quality captures and loops) first call waits until the code docs were handed over, in parts past one room - the main session reviewing without an edit never meets the edit hold; a seat's Skill call passes A design run's (task-design, issue-diagnoser, task-build-from-scratch) chat load is handed the code docs as additionalContext and never denied: one room, the rest named one read line each, only what was pasted whole marked, so the first scoped edit still hands the rest.

a typed run emits no Skill call (code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks: typing /name bypasses PreToolUse) - its expansion records the run, and a typed review is handed the code docs as a judge's start is, the rest with the main session's first reads; the matcher keeps every other prompt from spawning the hook; a typed design run (task-design, issue-diagnoser, task-build-from-scratch) is handed them the same way, never held

seeded OFF (ALFRED_CODE_TURN_CHECK=0): the turn's changed files from git (mtime past the previous Stop's marker), then ONE scoped tsc / dotnet build per root, first 20 error lines as a block, once per turn; it runs inside history-session's Stop process where that row is wired (2026-10-16: no node start of its own), its timeout 60 moving onto that wiring

what the last sessions on this branch did and ruled, injected at start (ALFRED_CODE_HISTORY sessions, seeded 3, at most 10; 150 chars plus 150 each) - engine history.js copied beside it; ALFRED_CODE_HISTORY=0 off; writes this session's session-inspector status file (.claude/session-inspector/status/<id>.json under its cwd, schema 1), prunes those past 7 days, keeps the folder out of git through info/exclude
records this session: commits, files left dirty, the user's AskUserQuestion answers - machine-local, <data root>/state/history/; rewrites the status file when a value changed

one line of forge facts at start (no network): the remote's host and kind, the forge CLIs on PATH, the MCP servers that are forge servers by their launch command or URL (never their name) and whether the ref watch is on - the model maps each concept onto the tool it has and never guesses the remote; engine forge.js beside it
the same forge line for a dispatched subagent - SessionStart context never reaches one at dispatch, and a seat that merges or watches a pipeline needs the same facts

the ref watch's PostToolUse: every call confirms the act the commit guard ledgered for it (an act never confirmed covers nothing), and one that could move a ref marks the cycle for the Stop's diff, a seat's calls included; the strong window: after a shell call forge.js reads as a merge, a branch write, a release or a forge call it cannot read, every branch and tag is re-read with git ls-remote and diffed against the session's baseline; a loud move no ledger act covers (the default branch, the upstream, a branch GIT-PREFERENCES.md names, a commit in this checkout, a tag) blocks with feedback to stop and report it
the same strong window after a call on any MCP server - an unknown tool that merged is caught right after it ran

the ref watch's catch-all: when the turn ran anything but a known read (a script, a seat, a browser click, an unknown tool) or a PostToolUse marked the cycle, and again after a turn that left background work running, every branch and tag is diffed once more - a loud move blocks once per cycle, the rest is one summary line for the user; an unreachable remote is 'not checked', never clean; forge-session:watch in ALFRED_CODE_HOOKS_OFF turns it off, ALFRED_CODE_FORGE_WATCH=loud-only drops the summary; a check that fails or takes over 3s pauses the catch-all for 30 min (a turn that made a forge call or a gated push still checks), and publish-only holds it to those turns
wired env-gated: a plain node spawn that exits at its own env check unless ALFRED_CODE_INSTRUMENT=1 (seeded "0" in .variables - flip it for a measured run; see README)

plugins.note: inline Roslyn diagnostics on edit (complements the navigation server nav); needs csharp-ls (dotnet tool install -g csharp-ls, on the .NET 10 SDK since csharp-ls 0.28.0 - /alfred-code:init installs it); pin: the official marketplace entry's version - the package itself is empty, and the server is whatever csharp-ls is on PATH, unpinned

same for Angular/TS work; needs typescript-language-server with a TypeScript 6 beside it (npm install -g typescript-language-server typescript@6 - TypeScript 7 ships no tsserver.js, and typescript-language-server 6 needs Node 22.22.2 or later; /alfred-code:init installs it); pin: the official marketplace entry's version - the server is whatever typescript-language-server is on PATH, unpinned

statusline HUD - optional since 2.2.0, recommended in every install (meta/recommendations.json always.plugins), at the scope the user picks for it (this project by default; a project-scope one gets its status line in the project's settings.local.json); pin: a third-party marketplace, its plugin.json version - auto-update is off there by default, so the stack's update is what moves it
